Des civils yéménites suivent le convoi de prisonniers à bord de camionnettes, formant une procession vers Sanaa après la prise de contrôle par les Houthis de la ville portuaire du sud de la mer Rouge. Ce semblant d’efficacité est obtenu au prix d’un pouvoir autoritaire voire féroce, qui viole les droits humains et s’attaque en particulier aux femmes. Le niveau élevé de corruption qui ponctionne l’aide humanitaire internationale dont dépendent les trois quarts des Yéménites, offre des ressources au pouvoir en place. 8 — Une alliance avec l’Iran L’appréhension du mouvement houthiste est parfois réduite à son intégration dans la politique régionale iranienne dont il ne serait qu’une marionnette ou, un proxy . Les liens entre le mouvement yéménite et la République islamique ne sont pas un mystère. Ils s’ancrent dans les origines du mouvement houthiste il y a plus de vingt ans. Mais il convient de ne pas les surévaluer. La circulation d’un savoir-faire militaire, le transfert de composants pour fabriquer des drones ou des missiles de longue portée ainsi que des financements probables font des houthistes un relais efficace, mobilisé à moindre coût par les dirigeants iraniens International Affairs , Volume 92, Issue 3, May 2016, Pages 647–663'> 10 . Toutefois, leur grille de lecture régionale et leur stratégie s'inscrivent avant tout dans le contexte historique yéménite. Les dirigeants du mouvement ont toujours veillé à justifier leurs actions en fonction de la situation locale et à modifier le rapport de force avec leurs ennemis directs. C’est ainsi qu'il faut comprendre leur retenue sur le détroit de Bab el-Mandeb pendant les premiers mois de la guerre américano-israélienne déclenchée en février 2026. Ils ne souhaitaient en aucun cas apparaître aux yeux de leurs partisans comme agissant au nom des intérêts de l’Iran. Des combattants Houthis participent à une manifestation pour protester contre les frappes israéliennes sur Gaza et Sanaa le 25 août 2026. Les troupes armées sont suivies par une foule de soutien. Des combattants Houthis participent à une manifestation pour protester contre les frappes israéliennes sur Gaza et Sanaa le 25 août 2026. Les troupes armées sont suivies par une foule de soutien. 9 — Un double engagement : Palestine et Arabie saoudite L’ancrage local et le lien avec la politique régionale iranienne guident un engagement constant contre l’Arabie saoudite et Israël, ou plutôt en soutien aux Palestiniens. L’offensive saoudienne contre les houthistes, qui a débuté en 2015, a progressivement donné lieu à des mesures de rétorsion significatives, à mesure que les capacités de projection militaire de ces derniers se sont accrues. Drones puis missiles de longue portée ont, à compter de 2019, placé des villes et des infrastructures saoudiennes à portée de tir. Cet état de fait a favorisé une stratégie de retrait et de négociation avec les Houthistes chez les dirigeants saoudiens, ce qui a conduit au cessez-le-feu de mars 2022, en vigueur sous une forme ou une autre jusqu’en août 2026. Pendant cette période où le conflit semblait gelé, les houthistes ont constamment fait monter les enchères, formulant notamment des exigences financières que les Saoudiens ne pouvaient pas accepter. Au cours de l’été 2026, après que les Houthistes eurent cherché à mettre les Saoudiens devant le fait accompli en autorisant l’arrivée d’un avion en provenance de Téhéran, les Saoudiens ont de nouveau bombardé l’aéroport de Sanaa. En représailles, les houthistes ont annoncé un blocus des navires à destination de l’Arabie saoudite. Cette décision a alors justifié leur offensive contre le détroit de Bab el-Mandeb, marquant le début d'une nouvelle phase de la guerre, avec des attaques ciblant l'aéroport de Riyad et les pipelines saoudiens. L’engagement des houthistes en faveur de la Palestine est ancien et donne lieu à des manifestations massives qui sont bien davantage qu’une instrumentalisation du conflit israélo-arabe, tant elles servent leur popularité. Suite aux attaques du 7 octobre 2023 et aux bombardements israéliens sur Gaza, les houthistes ont investi un terrain militaire qui semblait longtemps hors de portée de ces combattants venus des montagnes : la mer Rouge. Dès novembre 2023, ils ont annoncé cibler les navires commerciaux liés, même indirectement, à Israël. Cette stratégie a désorganisé le commerce maritime mondial, mais a aussi occasionné des bombardements israéliens et américains. En mai 2025, Donald Trump a fini par signer un accord avec les houthistes, tandis que les Israéliens continuaient de mener des raids aériens en réponse aux envois de drones et de missiles sur Israël et aux attaques contre les navires longeant les côtes yéménites. Bien que les bombardements israéliens aient été significatifs, conduisant notamment à l’assassinat de douze ministres du gouvernement houthiste en août 2025, le mouvement yéménite n’a jamais semblé réellement affaibli Mediterranean Politics .'> 11 . Une vidéo de propagande montre des combattants houthis prenant d’assaut le cargo israélien Galaxy Leader, le 19 novembre 2023. Le cargo intercepté dans la mer Rouge a été transformé en attraction touristique. Une vidéo de propagande montre des combattants houthis prenant d’assaut le cargo israélien Galaxy Leader, le 19 novembre 2023. Le cargo intercepté dans la mer Rouge a été transformé en attraction touristique. 10 — Des ennemis fragmentés La capacité militaire des houthistes et leur assise politique sont inversement proportionnelles à la division de leurs adversaires. Tant au niveau local qu’au niveau régional, le camp anti-houthiste n’a jamais réussi à former un front uni face aux avancées d’Ansar Allah. Dès les guerres de Sa'dah au milieu des années 2000, l’offensive contre les houthistes avait été instrumentalisée par les successeurs putatifs du président Saleh pour s'affaiblir mutuellement. À partir de 2015, les tensions entre Frères musulmans et partisans de la sécession sudiste, entre Arabie saoudite et Émirats arabes unis, ou entre milices originaires de l’est et du sud ont grandement grevé les capacités militaires du camp hostile aux houthistes. C'est cette fragmentation même, bien davantage que le soutien iranien, qui explique le succès à Bab el-Mandeb en septembre 2026 et leur capacité à tenir, depuis douze ans, les régions qu’ils contrôlent. L’article Les clefs de la puissance houthiste est apparu en premier sur Le Grand Continent .

items.title: Pourquoi Trump accueille-t-il Xi Jinping avec un fastueux protocole ?
items.description: Xi Jinping se rend aujourd'hui aux États-Unis pour la sixième fois depuis son arrivée au pouvoir, en 2013. Pour la première fois, il sera accueilli par le président américain dès la sortie de l’avion, en rupture avec le protocole, qui prévoit dans la quasi-totalité des visites d’État de dirigeants étrangers une cérémonie de bienvenue sur la pelouse sud de la Maison-Blanche. Trump deviendra ainsi le premier président depuis Kennedy à se rendre à l’Andrews Air Force Base pour accueillir un homologue – en-dehors de visites papales Protocol, Agenda and Potential Outcomes of the Trump-Xi Summit », China Tech Bite , 22 septembre 2026.'> 12 . Le dispositif déployé par la Maison-Blanche en l’honneur de Xi Jinping et de la première dame, Peng Liyuan, dépasse les moyens mis en place lors de la visite de Trump à Pékin, en mai. Après un accueil à l’Andrews Air Force Base, Trump recevra Xi à la Maison-Blanche demain, jeudi 24. À cette occasion, 479 militaires représentant toutes les branches des forces armées américaines seront présents sur la pelouse sud. La cérémonie comprendra un salut présidentiel rendu par le peloton de drill silencieux des Marines des États-Unis et le Commandement des forces interarmées des États-Unis, et s'achèvera par un survol militaire mettant en scène un bombardier furtif B-2 Spirit et quatre chasseurs furtifs F-22 Raptors. Xi est habitué à être reçu dès la sortie de son avion par ses hôtes. Ces dernières années, les dirigeants qui ont fait le déplacement à cette occasion incluent l'ancien Premier ministre hongrois Viktor Orbán, le roi du Cambodge Norodom Sihamoni, le président serbe Aleksandar Vučić et le dirigeant nord-coréen Kim Jong-un. Ces honneurs sont toutefois rarement rendus : le protocole diplomatique chinois prévoit en effet un accueil par des ministres ou des hauts-responsables. Le chancelier allemand Friedrich Merz avait ainsi été accueilli à Pékin lors de sa visite en février 2026, tandis que l'ancien Premier ministre britannique Keir Starmer avait été reçu à l'aéroport par le ministre chinois des Finances, Lan Fo'an, en janvier. Trump lui-même avait été accueilli par le vice-président Han Zheng, et non pas par Xi Jinping. La rencontre vise avant tout à consolider l'entente amorcée à Busan en octobre 2025, puis prolongée à Pékin en mai. Pour Rush Doshi, ancien haut responsable au Conseil de sécurité nationale sous Biden, Busan a surtout démontré que la Chine se considérait désormais comme l’égal des États-Unis dans de nombreux domaines (IA, commerce, sécurité…) The Moment China Proved It Was America’s Equal », The New York Times , 19 novembre 2025.'> 13 Pékin a répliqué aux droits de douane américains en arsenalisation sa domination du secteur des terres rares, forçant Washington à reculer. Le fastueux protocole réservé à Xi s'inscrit dans cette dynamique de courtoisie intéressée – Washington cherche ainsi moins à impressionner Pékin qu'à s'assurer de sa coopération. La visite d’État doit permettre de maintenir la dynamique des relations et de confirmer deux nouvelles rencontres avant la fin de l’année : l'une lors du sommet de l’APEC à Shenzhen, en novembre, et l’autre au G20 à Miami, en décembre. L’objectif principal est de préserver ce cadre de « stabilité stratégique constructive ». Les deux parties ont en effet intérêt à prolonger la trêve commerciale, compte tenu des cycles politiques internes : les élections de mi-mandat aux États-Unis en novembre et le congrès du Parti communiste chinois, à l’automne 2027. L’article Pourquoi Trump accueille-t-il Xi Jinping avec un fastueux protocole ? est apparu en premier sur Le Grand Continent .

items.title: Asian Development Bank keeps Pakistan's growth forecast at 3.7pc
items.description: ISLAMABAD: The Asian Development Bank (ADB) on Wednesday forecast Pakistan’s economic growth rate at 3.7 per cent — lower than the 4pc budget target — and inflation at 8.3pc — higher than the official estimate of 7pc for the current fiscal year — amid downside risks stemming from the conflict in the Middle East. “Pakistan’s gross domestic product growth is projected to remain at 3.7pc in FY2027”, the Manila-based lending agency said in its Asian Development Outlook September episode. In its latest outlook, ADB has maintained its July forecast of 3.7pc. It had earlier projected a 4.5pc growth rate for the current fiscal year in its April 2026 forecast. “Average inflation is projected to rise to 8.3pc in FY27, above the central bank’s medium-term target range of 5pc–7pc, as elevated energy, logistics, and agricultural input costs continue to affect domestic prices”, it added. The bank warned that the economic outlook was subject to significant downside risks. An escalation of the Middle East conflict could increase energy import costs, intensify inflation, and disrupt labour markets in Gulf economies, affecting workers’ remittances. “The reintroduction of austerity measures by the Pakistan government could also weigh on domestic demand and economic activity, particularly if expenditure restraint is more pronounced than anticipated, posing an additional downside risk to the economic outlook”, the ADB noted. It also highlighted other risks including tighter global financing conditions, shortfalls in tax revenue, weather-related agricultural shocks, and delays in energy-sector and state-owned enterprise reforms. The ADB emphasised consistent implementation of reforms as critical to reinforcing fiscal and external stability and sustaining investor confidence. It noted that Pakistan’s economic performance continued to strengthen in fiscal year 2026 (FY26, ended 30 June 2026), with growth accelerating to 3.7pc from 3.2pc in FY25. The expansion was broad-based, supported by resilient services, a rebound in manufacturing, recovery in agriculture, and stronger private investment, although the Middle East conflict slowed economic activity in the final quarter of the fiscal year. Sustained implementation of economic reforms, improved external buffers, renewed access to international capital markets, and recent sovereign credit rating upgrades are expected to support investor confidence and private investment. However, elevated energy prices and continued external uncertainty, including lingering effects of the Middle East conflict, are expected to constrain further acceleration in growth. “Pakistan’s economy has made progress in strengthening macroeconomic stability over the past two years, with stronger growth, improved external buffers, restored market confidence, and sovereign credit rating upgrades reflecting the benefits of sustained reforms”, said ADB Country Director for Pakistan Emma Fan. “Maintaining reform momentum will be critical to unlock higher private investment, strengthen resilience to external shocks, and achieve stronger and more inclusive growth.“ Growth in FY26 was supported by expansion in manufacturing and services. Agriculture grew by 2.9pc, despite flood-related losses to major crops, while private investment increased by 8.6pc amid lower borrowing costs and improved business confidence, ADB said. Fiscal consolidation continued during FY26. Gross international reserves increased, strengthening external resilience. Pakistan’s sovereign credit ratings were upgraded by S&P in July 2026 and Moody’s in August 2026, reflecting improved macroeconomic stability, stronger external buffers, and continued reform implementation. Pakistan also regained access to international capital markets through Eurobond and Panda bond issuances in April and May 2026. Inflation averaged 7.1pc in FY26, compared with 4.5pc in FY25, as rising food prices and higher global oil prices intensified price pressures during the second half of the year.

items.title: IHC working on policy to rotate judges to other provinces
items.description: ISLAMABAD: The Islamabad High Court (IHC) administration has started working on a policy for rotation of judges of the subordinate judiciary to other provinces, a long-awaited demand of the capital’s legal fraternity that was accepted in principle by the National Judicial Policy Making Committee (NJPMC). Informed sources said several proposals were being considered to determine the modalities for implementing the inter-provincial rotation of judges of Islamabad’s district judiciary. One proposal under consideration is that judicial officers posted to other provinces should preferably be sent to the province from where they originally belong. The Islamabad judiciary comprises officers who joined the service through different modes, including initial appointments, absorption and deputation, and judicial officers from all four provinces are currently serving in the capital. The sources said there were around 60 judicial officers in the Islamabad judiciary, and the authorities were considering whether all of them, 50pc of them or one-third should be rotated to other provinces. Another issue under consideration is whether the rotation should cover all tiers of the subordinate judiciary — civil judges, senior civil judges, additional district and sessions judges and district and sessions judges — or be limited to certain categories. “Whatever formula is adopted, one thing is clear: the equal number of judges sent from Islamabad will be brought in from the provinces to maintain the strength of the district judiciary,” a legal expert familiar with the proposed mechanism said. The proposed policy follows a longstanding demand by Islamabad’s lawyers for giving the district judiciary of the federal capital the same opportunity for inter-provincial transfers and rotations available to judges in the provinces. In May, the Islamabad High Court Bar Association formally demanded a uniform transfer and rotation policy for the district judiciary. The NJPMC subsequently accepted the demand in principle and decided to introduce inter-provincial rotation of Islamabad’s subordinate judiciary. The move came after years of calls from the legal fraternity for greater institutional balance in the capital’s district courts. The issue has gained further significance following the transfer of three IHC judges to the Lahore, Peshawar and Sindh high courts earlier this year. Bar bodies had subsequently called for a structured and periodic rotation mechanism for judges rather than selective transfers. The concept of rotating Islamabad’s lower court judges is not new. In 2018, the federal government had proposed amendments to the Islamabad Judicial Service Rules to enable subordinate court judges to be sent on deputation to other provinces, while noting that the existing rules did not provide for such transfers. The proposed mechanism has, however, also generated apprehensions among some judicial officers. Concerns have been expressed that frequent movement between Islamabad and other provinces could expose judges to new forms of professional pressure, including attempts by lawyers to influence judicial decisions or pressure judges considered “non-cooperative”. The authorities are therefore faced with the task of devising a transparent and uniform mechanism that provides for inter-provincial exposure and rotation while safeguarding judicial independence and ensuring that the strength of Islamabad’s district judiciary remains intact. The final policy is expected to settle the number and categories of judges to be rotated, the duration of their postings and the procedure for replacing them with judicial officers from other provinces. Published in Dawn, September 23rd, 2026

items.title: La ley permite a las fundaciones recibir donaciones prohibidas a los partidos de los que dependen
items.description: La Ley de Financiación de Partidos Políticos les prohíbe aceptar donaciones procedentes de personas físicas por un importe superior a 50.000 euros al año y veta los donativos de personas jurídicas (entidades o empresas) cualquiera que sea la cuantía, para evitar que puedan condicionar su actividad política. Sin embargo, la fundación Disenso, vinculada a Vox, recibió en 2023 cuatro donaciones de personas físicas por un valor total de 232.300 euros, por lo que al menos una de ellas tuvo que superar necesariamente los 50.000 euros, mientras que la Pablo Iglesias, del PSOE, ingresó un único donativo de una persona jurídica por importe de 100.000 euros. Ambas son legales, y han sido avaladas por el Tribunal de Cuentas, ya que la misma ley exceptúa a las fundaciones de los límites que impone a los partidos de los que dependen. Seguir leyendo

items.title: AfD descoloca por sorpresa a la ultraderecha italiana al alentar el secesionismo del Tirol del sur
items.description: La derecha y la extrema derecha italiana se han topado con un problema incómodo donde menos lo esperaban, sobre todo aquellos que han saludado con entusiasmo el ascenso de AfD en Alemania , como La Liga de Matteo Salvini y Futuro Nacional, del exgeneral Roberto Vannacci . Porque resulta que el partido ultra alemán está soplando sobre una vieja y delicada cuestión, la secesión del sur del Tirol , un territorio del Imperio Austrohúngaro integrado en Italia desde 1920, en los acuerdos firmados tras la I Guerra Mundial. items.title: Manuela Bergerot: “Los ultrarricos y los acaparadores de vivienda son un gran peligro para nuestra democracia”
items.description: Manuela Bergerot no tiene miedo a subirse a la tribuna y a pronunciar una frase que espanta a los ricos que toman café en alguna de las terrazas de la Puerta de Alcalá. “ Vamos a expropiar a los propietarios de más de 10 viviendas”, dice detrás de sus gafas de concha y con una melena canosa que la hace reconocible a lo lejos. Bergerot (La Plata, Argentina, 50 años) forma parte de esta nueva izquierda que quiere desempolvar conceptos demonizados en el debate público como socialismo, redistribución de la riqueza y subida de impuestos, asuntos que se han asociado a dos hombres, uno con barba y el otro barbilampiño, los dos de uniforme, llamados Fidel Castro y Hugo Chávez. La portavoz de Más Madrid en la Asamblea de Madrid se encuentra más bien en la senda de Zohran Mamdani , el alcalde de Nueva York, socialista y musulmán, el nuevo fenómeno mundial del progresismo. Ella cree que por ese camino se puede vencer a Isabel Díaz Ayuso , la presidenta de Madrid, del PP, a quien retrata sentada a la mesa de los poderosos: “Ella gobierna por y para las grandes fortunas”. Seguir leyendo

items.title: El Supremo prevé levantar la orden de detención de Puigdemont cuando reciba el aval del Constitucional, que resolverá el 6 de octubre
items.description: El aval del Tribunal Constitucional a amnistiar el delito de malversación de los líderes del procés no es un simple paso más hacia la vuelta a España de Carles Puigdemont sin riesgo a ser detenido. El acuerdo adoptado este martes por el tribunal de garantías es una zancada casi definitiva que, salvo que haya un giro de guion de última hora, sitúa el regreso del expresidente de la Generalitat a la vuelta de la esquina. Si el Constitucional, como es previsible, aprueba el próximo 6 de octubre las sentencias favorables a amnistiar a los ex consejeros Jordi Turull y Dolors Bassa, que se votarán ese día, y los argumentos de esas resoluciones son extrapolables al resto de líderes independentistas, la intención del magistrado Pablo Llarena, instructor del procés , es levantar de forma inmediata la orden de detención que pesa contra Puigdemont sin esperar a que el Constitucional resuelva el recurso de amparo presentado por el expresident , cuya deliberación todavía no tiene fecha. Seguir leyendo

items.title: PPP rejects opposition’s long march to Islamabad
items.description: ISLAMABAD: Rejecting the opposition’s plan to stage a long march from Peshawar to the federal capital on Sept 27, the PPP has urged the opposition and the government to show mercy to the people and avoid any clash. “Frequent marches on Islamabad severely disrupt the lives of citizens,” said the party’s Secretary General Nayyer Hussain Bukhari in a statement on Tuesday. “Whether it is May 9 or Nov 26, the people ultimately suffer,” he added. Political clashes, he said, at the cost of the country and its people were unacceptable. Urges govt, political parties to avoid confrontation over Sept 27 protest “The government and the opposition must show mercy to the people and resolve political issues through dialogue,” Mr Bukhari said. He said repeated marches and confrontations in Islamabad severely affected the lives of citizens and disrupted normal economic and social activities. He said that, whether it was May 9 or November 26, ordinary people were ultimately forced to face difficulties and disruptions. “Political confrontation and violence at the cost of the country and its people are unacceptable,” he added. Mr Bukhari urged both the government and the opposition to show consideration for the people and focus on political stability, economic development and resolution of public issues. He said the prevailing circumstances demand that both sides demonstrate political maturity and prioritise the national interest. The PPP leader said the government and opposition should abandon stubbornness and adopt the path of dialogue. “Political issues cannot be resolved through confrontation, force or agitation; they must be addressed through negotiations and constitutional and democratic means,” he added. Mr Bukhari said Pakistan was neither a monarchy nor could a monarchical system function in the country. “Pakistan must be governed according to the Constitution, law and democratic principles,” he said. Expressing concern over rising petroleum prices, he said it was surprising that petrol prices in Pakistan were increasing day by day despite declining prices in the international market. The increase in petroleum prices and inflation have made life extremely difficult for the poor. “The government must take effective measures to provide relief to the public,” he demanded. Mr Bukhari said under the Constitution, the federal government could seek assistance from the provinces, including police personnel when required. “The Constitution provides a framework for cooperation between the federation and the provinces, and constitutional procedures should be followed,” he added. “Nelson Mandela was released as a result of negotiations, not by breaking out of prison. The political challenges in Pakistan should likewise be addressed through dialogue, the Constitution and parliament,” he said. Published in Dawn, September 23rd, 2026

items.title: Medical tribunal grants relief to 2 suspended medics
items.description: • Both were among five trainees involved in recording ‘educational video’ during surgery at Lady Willingdon Hospital • Post-grad trainees allowed to appear in final exams ISLAMABAD: In two significant interim orders drawing a distinction between professional discipline and the pursuit of education, a medical tribunal on Tuesday allowed two postgraduate doctors, who face two-year suspension of their medical licences, to continue postgraduate training and appear in their forthcoming final examinations, while their appeals against disciplinary action remain pending. The three-member tribunal, headed by retired Justice Safdar Saleem Shahid, granted identical interim relief to Dr Tayyaba Fatima Toor and Dr Muhammad Essa, suspending the operation of the Pakistan Medical and Dental Council disciplinary order dated July 28, 2026, but only to the extent necessary to enable them to continue and complete their postgraduate academic and training programmes and appear in their final postgraduate examinations. The tribunal was careful, however, not to disturb the disciplinary findings at this stage or restore an unrestricted licence to practise medicine. It expressly clarified that the interim arrangement was provisional, subject to the final outcome of the appeals, and did not amount to an adjudication permitting the appellants to undertake independent clinical practice. The two doctors were among five postgraduate trainees whose cases attracted considerable attention following the circulation of what became known as the “ OT video leak scandal ” at Lahore’s Lady Willingdon Hospital. In April this year, the PMDC had publicly stated that five doctors — Dr Tayyaba Fatima Toor, Dr Zainab Tahir, Dr Muhammad Essa, Dr Ayesha Afzal and Dr Maham Amin — had appeared in preliminary proceedings concerning a video circulating on social media. The council subsequently referred the matter to its Disciplinary Committee for final determination. The disciplinary proceedings eventually resulted in the suspension of the medical registration licences of the appellants for two years. That decision is now under challenge before the Medical Tribunal, and Tuesday’s orders concern only the doctors’ applications for interim relief, rather than the merits of their appeals. “Material distinction” At the centre of the tribunal’s reasoning is a distinction likely to have wider relevance for disciplinary proceedings involving doctors who are simultaneously postgraduate trainees. The tribunal held that there was a “material distinction” between permission to pursue an academic programme and appear in an examination, on the one hand, and permission independently to practise medicine under a professional licence, on the other. The former, it observed, could, in an appropriate case, be protected provisionally without finally determining the latter. The distinction enabled the tribunal to preserve the regulatory authority of the PMDC while ensuring that the pendency of an appeal did not itself cause academic consequences that could become irreversible before the legality of the disciplinary action had been finally determined. According to the orders, counsel informed the tribunal that the appellants had already substantially completed their prescribed postgraduate training and cleared the requisite intermediate or mid-term component. Their final postgraduate examinations were stated to be due in approximately four months. The tribunal observed that if the doctors were prevented from completing the remaining academic component and consequently missed their forthcoming examinations, success in their appeals at a later stage might not adequately restore the academic opportunity already lost. Conversely, it held, permitting them provisionally to continue their academic programmes and sit the examinations would neither determine the validity of the disciplinary proceedings nor confer an unconditional right to practice medicine during the pendency of their appeals. The cases will now proceed on their merits before the medical tribunal. Published in Dawn, September 23rd, 2026

items.title: El Gobierno estudia una intervención de los precios del gas para frenar la subida de la factura eléctrica
items.description: El Gobierno tiene encima de la mesa una “inevitable” intervención del mercado mayorista de la electricidad ( pool ) ante el temor a un repunte aún mayor de los precios del gas natural, según indican fuentes políticas y empresariales. El pool es un mercado de precios marginales en el que, una vez que desaparece la luz del sol y, con ella, la producción fotovoltaica, marcan precio las centrales más caras, las de ciclo combinado de gas, y es el que cobran también el resto de las energías (nuclear, hidráulica y otras renovables). Las mismas fuentes apuntan a que el Ejecutivo, entre las posibles medidas disponibles y presionado por sus socios de Sumar, estaría analizando la posibilidad de recuperar la llamada excepción ibérica, que España aplicó a partir de 2024, tras la crisis energética derivada de la invasión rusa de Ucrania y una dura y larga negociación con la Comisión Europea. Dicho mecanismo, que estuvo vigente durante un año, implicaba una subvención o ayuda de Estado que aceptó a regañadientes Bruselas. Seguir leyendo

items.title: IHC seeks Pakistan Medical and Dental Council view on doctors’ working hours
items.description: • Terms 102-hour work week for medics ‘inhuman’ • CPSP cites international limits, including 48 hours per week in Europe, 80 hours in US ISLAMABAD: The Islamabad High Court (IHC) on Tuesday direc­ted the Pakistan Medical and Dental Council (PMDC) to examine the issue of excessive working hours for doctors and place its recommendations before the government, observing that requiring doctors to work up to 102 hours a week was inhuman. Justice Raja Inaam Ameen Min­has heard at length a petition concerning the working hours of doctors and, with the consent of the parties, converted the writ petition into a representation before the PMDC. The court directed the PMDC to decide the representation and place its recommendations before the federal and provincial governments for appropriate action. The issue assumes significance as comments submitted by the College of Physicians and Surgeons Pakistan (CPSP) before the court have highlighted the serious consequences of prolonged duty hours for both doctors and patients. According to the CPSP material placed before the court, after approximately 18 hours of work, doctors develop psychomotor dysfunction equivalent to a blood alcohol level of 0.05. At 24 hours of continuous duty, the impairment was stated to be equivalent to a blood alcohol level of 0.1. The document questioned the safety of expecting an exhausted doctor to make critical decisions or perform medical procedures after such prolonged duty. The CPSP comments also state that tired doctors make more mistakes than doctors who are fresh, alert and properly supervised. The stated objective, according to the document, should therefore be to reduce working hours to a level that allows for a healthy work-life balance for staff and ensures safe care for patients. The material submitted before the court refers to international practices governing doctors’ working hours. It says the European Working Time Directive provides for a maximum average working week of 48 hours, at least 11 consecutive hours of daily rest and minimum weekly rest periods. In the US, the document notes a maximum of 80 duty hours per week, averaged over four weeks, along with a minimum of one day free of patient-care responsibilities in seven days and limits on continuous duty. The CPSP document further states that in India, following directions from the Supreme Court, junior residents should ordinarily work 48 hours a week and not more than 12 hours at a stretch, while a total of 48 hours per week has been prescribed. In Iran, the Iranian Council for Graduate Medical Education has determined a minimum of 50 hours per week, with restrictions on night duties. The CPSP itself has recommended that residency programmes require a minimum of 48 duty hours per week for clinical specialties, excluding emergency duties and Sundays on call. It also states that a trainee should not be required to undertake more than two night or emergency duties of 12 hours each in a week, while trainees assigned to emergency departments should not work shifts exceeding 12 hours. Interestingly, the CPSP clarified in its para-wise comments that it does not employ doctors and, therefore, does not prescribe their working hours, which fall within the domain of the respective provincial governments or private organisations. It said its role relates to the training programmes conducted at accredited institutions. The document also notes that there is considerable variation in the implementation of limits on doctors’ actual working hours, working conditions and the level of supervision available to young doctors. It points out that reducing the duty hours of resident doctors would require health facilities to arrange additional doctors to cover the workload. It further observes that fatigue does not depend solely on the number of hours worked but also on environmental conditions. The CPSP material refers to hot weather, non-air-conditioned workplaces and other environmental factors that may aggravate physical and mental fatigue. Published in Dawn, September 23rd, 2026

items.title: Pa­­kistan Single Window enables remote biometric verification via Nadra’s PakID App
items.description: THE facility will also be useful for overseas Pakis­tanis involved in trade-related activities at home.—Online ISLAMABAD: The Pa­­kistan Single Window (PSW) has integrated its platform with the National Database and Registra­tion Authority’s (Nadra) PakID Mobile App, allowing users to complete mandatory biometric verification remotely through their smartphones. The new facility enables PSW users to complete biometric verification for subscription, subscription renewal and profile updates without having to physically visit Nadra’s e-Sahulat Centre. Previously, biometric ver­­ification for PSW services required users to ap­­pear in person at Nadra’s e-Sahulat Centre. Follow­ing the integration with the PakID Mobile App, eligible users can now complete the verification process remo­tely, subject to applicable Nadra requirements. The facility is expected to be particularly convenient for overseas Pakis­tanis involved in trade-related activities in the country. Eligible overseas users will be able to complete their PSW biometric verification remotely through the PakID app, reducing the need for physical visits to Pakistan for this purpose. To facilitate a smooth transition, both verification channels will remain available during an interim period. Users will therefore have the option of completing their biometric verification digitally through the PakID Mobile App or continuing to visit Nadra e-Sahulat Centres. “The integration with Nadra’s PakID Mobile App reflects our commitment to listening to the PSW community both in Pakistan and overseas and responding to their needs,” said Syed Aftab Haider, CEO of PSW. “By enabling remote biometric verification, we are removing another phy­­sical trip in the on­boarding process and making the PSW user journey more convenient, accessible, and user driven,” he added. According to PSW, the integration removes the only physical visit previously required during the subscription process, enabling the entire process to be completed digitally. The initiative is part of PSW’s broader efforts to expand the use of digital solutions, improve accessibility and simplify procedures for businesses. Published in Dawn, September 23rd, 2026

items.title: Saudi king denounces Houthis in rare rebuke
items.description: • Rebels accuse Riyadh of deadly strikes as thousands flee • 154 people reportedly killed in fighting over past two days • G7 calls on Yemeni group to halt military actions, attacks on shipping • UK commits air-to-air refuelling support for Saudis SANAA: The king of Saudi Arabia denounced Yemen’s Houthis as a “terrorist militia” in a rare statement on Tue­sday reacting to an attack that authorities said targeted the holy city of Makkah last week. King Salman, 90, praised the armed forces and security services for defending the country, and condemned the recent Houthi attempt “to target Makkah”, calling it “a provocation to Muslims aro­u­nd the world”, according to the official Saudi news agency. Houthis also accused Saudi Arabia on Tuesday of launching a wave of deadly strikes that killed civilians and prison inmates, as Riyadh seeks to repel an offensive that has seen the Iran-backed group seize strategic territory. The recent Houthi takeover of Yemen’s Red Sea coast has left hundreds dead and heightened fears over global trade and shipping through the vital Bab al-Mandab strait. It has also forced thousands to flee, with the United Nations on Tuesday forecasting the number of displaced could swell from over 130,000 today to more than 230,000 in the coming months. The gains made by the Houthis have cemented the hold of Iran and its regional allies over two key waterways in the Middle East — and the straits of Bab al-Mandab and Hormuz — which are major shipping arteries for global flows of energy. Saudi Arabia, which backs Yemen’s internationally recognised government, has sought to contain the Houthi advance with air strikes. The Houthis have retaliated with attacks on Saudi territory, including a strike targeting the capital Riyadh for the first time in years. The strike came days after Saudi Arabia accused the Houthis of targeting the holy city of Makkah, though the fighters denied the claim. In Yemen, the Houthis said a strike on a prison killed nine detainees, while they also accused the Saudis of killing six civilians including two children in the port city of Mocha. Two more civilians were killed by strikes in Yemen’s Al-Jawf province, the Houthis added. “A mother and child were killed, while her husband and two of her other children were wounded in strikes carried out by the Saudi enemy” in the Al-Batin area, Houthi media said, citing the Houthi health ministry. ‘Humiliation’ As violence has escalated, thousands of families have been forced from their homes, many for a second or third time. “I hope I can find a house to live in with my children. We are exhausted by the heat, the dust and the humiliation,” Arwa, a mother of four children, told AFP at a camp for displaced people near Aden. Fighting between the Houthis and Saudi-backed Yemeni forces has in the past two days killed 154 people, military sources from both sides told AFP . “The death toll from Saudi air strikes, clashes and artillery fire in the governorates of Taiz, Al-Jawf, Marib and Saada stands at 118,” Houthi military sources said, while government sources reported 36 killed in their ranks. Saudi Arabia’s civil defence age­n­­cy on Tuesday issued a warning of potential danger in the country’s sou­th near the Yemen border, the first alert since the Houthis launched their attack on Riyadh over the weekend. The alert, which asked people to remain indoors and avoid open areas, was lifted a short while later. UK, French support G7 leaders representing Canada, France, Germany, Italy, Japan, the United Kingdom and the United States called on the Houthis to “immediately cease all military actions”. They also demanded the Houthis end “all threats and attacks against civilian shipping, and to return to the political process in good faith”, while urging Tehran “to end its arming of and support for the Houthis”. Britain has also agreed to provide some military support to Saudi Arabia, defence minister Luke Pollard said. A British tanker plane will provide “defensive” air-to-air refuelling for Saudi warplanes to help the country defend against Houthi strikes, the UK government confirmed late Monday. “We’re doing it for national security reasons in support of our own national security,” Pollard told Sky News. “In dangerous times, good friends stand together,” he added, insisting the support would be in compliance with international humanitarian law. France also pledged to help secure Saudi energy infrastructure, a diplomatic source said. But “this in no way involves taking part in the conflict with the Houthis”, the French source said. The Houthis have carried out attacks against facilities belonging to Saudi oil giant Aramco in the Red Sea port city of Yanbu. Yemen’s government and Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Sal­man have reportedly requested help from US President Donald Trump in fighting the Houthis. More displacement feared Renewed fighting in Yemen could see the number of refugees fleeing across the Red Sea to Djibouti jump to 10,000, while displacement inside Yemen could swell to over 230,000, the UN warned on Tuesday. More than 100,000 civilians have been uprooted inside Yemen while others have risked dangerous sea crossings to flee the violence. “Intensifying fighting in Yemen could drive more mass displacement,” United Nations refugee agency spokesman Babar Baloch told reporters. Published in Dawn, September 23rd, 2026

items.title: Pakistan stands out amid flurry of diplomacy at UNGA
items.description: • As Islamabad presses Washington and Tehran to return to talks, Trump reveals ‘three-hour meeting’ with Iranian delegation • US president hails PM Shehbaz as ‘terrific man’; diplomatic efforts win praise from UN chief • Dar joins counterparts from Turkiye, Saudi Arabia and Egypt in stressing need to uphold Islamabad MoU NEW YORK: Pakistan remained front and centre on Tuesday, amid a flurry of diplomatic activity at UN Headquarters, as world leaders came together to address the 81st General Assembly session. Both PM Shehbaz Sharif and Deputy PM Ishaq Dar spent a busy day filled with whirlwind meetings, engaging with leaders from around the world, as they continued to push for a diplomatic solution to the US-Iran war, which has taken a toll on global trade and energy markets. Although he is scheduled to address the UNGA tomorrow (Thursday), PM Shehbaz was mentioned by US President Donald Trump in his speech, who called him a “terrific man”. “The prime minister of Pakistan — terrific man — said that Donald Trump was responsible for saving 30 million lives and probably many more than that,” he said as he rattled off a list of conflicts that he claimed to have helped settle: Pakistan-India, Thailand-Cambodia, Armenia-Azerbaijan, and the Gaza conflict, among others. Pakistan has been vigorously pursuing diplomacy to help bring the United States and Iran back to the negotiating table, even as uncertainty clouded a possible meeting between Trump and Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian on the sidelines of the UNGA. Those efforts seem to have borne fruit when, after sending mixed signals during his UNGA speech, President Trump said that his team had met an Iranian delegation on the sidelines of the General Assembly. “It was a meeting that lasted for three hours; it ended an hour ago,” Trump told reporters after a meeting with Ukrainian President Volodomyr Zelensky. “It was a very good meeting. I can’t imagine why they wouldn’t want to do it; it’s greatness or obliteration.” He added that the meeting was “productive” and that “They have another one scheduled in the very near future”. According to diplomatic sources at the United Nations, Pakistan has been “quietly but persistently urging” both Washington and Tehran to maintain indirect contacts and “remain positively open” to direct talks. A day earlier, Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi had travelled to Tehran and met Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian and Iranian Interior Minister Eskandar Momeni, with the mediation process among the issues discussed. During the visit, Iranian officials expressed appreciation for Pakistan’s continuing efforts to promote regional peace and stability. The diplomatic efforts were also appreciated by Secretary-General António Guterres, whose spokesperson said a day earlier that the outgoing UN chief was “very grateful and appreciative” of the efforts by Pakistan’s leadership to mediate between Washington and Tehran and help end the violence. Guterres’ spokesman Stéphane Dujarric told a news briefing in New York that Pakistan’s role was “critical”, and described the understanding reached in Islamabad as “a great achievement.” He said Guterres had remained in close touch with the Pakistani leadership as part of efforts to achieve the shared objective of ending the conflict. Asked about the efforts of Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif and Pakistan’s army chief to mediate between Iran and the United States, Dujarric said the UN chief appreciated the Pakistani leadership’s efforts to bring an end to the violence. “Other countries have also been involved,” he said, “but I think Pakistan’s role has been critical.” Dujarric also endorsed renewed direct engagement between Washington and Tehran, saying the UN “always” supports dialogue. “Diplomacy is our middle name, so to speak,” he said, adding that any re-engagement between the United States and Iran, as they had previously pursued, could help bring an end to the conflict, which he said was “hurting a lot of people.” Iranian President Pezeshkian is expected to address the UN General Assembly today (Wednesday) and hold bilateral meetings with world leaders. Marco Rubio said on Tuesday that no meeting with Iranian representatives was currently scheduled, but that Washington was open to such talks if they had the prospect of producing a positive result. Iran, meanwhile, has signalled that its delegation in New York has authority to pursue diplomacy. Tehran has also conveyed proposals to Washington through mediators, keeping open the possibility of a return to negotiations. Sideline meetings On Tuesday, Deputy PM Dar participated in a key ministerial meeting of the Regional-4 (R-4) group, where he was joined by the foreign ministers of Turkiye, Saudi Arabia, and Egypt. The R-4 group has been focused on regional security and emerged in March amid efforts for mediation between the US and Iran. As the group met in New York, DPM Dar reaffirmed “Pakistan’s strong commitment to the R-4 framework and expressed the need for continued engagement for enhancing regional peace and prosperity”, the Foreign Office (FO) said in a statement. It added that the participants exchanged views on the latest situation in the region and expressed full support for efforts aimed at a peaceful resolution of the situation. A statement issued by the Permanent Mission of Pakistan to the UN said that the ministers’ consultative meeting on Sept 21 on the sidelines of the session also discussed recent regional and international developments. “The ministers underscored that dialogue and diplomacy remain the only path towards sustainable resolution, and in this context they underscored the need for upholding the Islamabad Memorandum of Understanding for lasting peace and stability,” the statement said. Meanwhile, PM Shehbaz met with several world leaders, including President of Somalia Hassan Sheikh Mohamud, Austrian Chancellor Christian Stocker, Kenyan President William Ruto, and Kuwaiti crown prince Sheikh Sabah Khaled Al-Hamad Al-Sabah. Published in Dawn, September 23rd, 2026

items.title: Fresh fixing claims surface in Indian cricket after sting
items.description: NEW DELHI: A sting operation conducted by the Indian magazine Tehelka has cast a fresh spotlight on alleged match-fixing and the leaking of sensitive team information in Indian cricket, with a former Ranji Trophy player claiming involvement in both the Indian Premier League and domestic T20 leagues. In the undercover footage, Nagaland pacer and former Delhi school cricketer Rachit Bhatia is seen alleging that he fixed matches and passed confidential playing XIs to bookmakers. According to the report, Bhatia claimed he shared Indian Premier League (IPL) side Chennai Super Kings’ team details with London-based bookies via Snapchat before the toss during the 2025 IPL season, asserting he earned large sums in the process. He also spoke of similar activities in the Delhi Premier League and other state competitions, as well as accepting payments from parents to secure places for children in age-group sides. These claims, which have not been verified by any competent authority, have once again raised concerns about the vulnerability of franchise and lower-tier cricket in India to corrupt approaches. The Delhi and District Cricket Association responded on Tuesday to the controversy surrounding the recently concluded Delhi Premier League. A senior DDCA official confirmed to Press Trust of India (PTI) news agency that only one corrupt approach related to match-fixing had been reported to the league’s Anti-Corruption Unit during the tournament. “Central Delhi’s Vansh Bedi was approached by a fixer and he immediately reported the matter to the ACU,” the official was quoted as saying by PTI. Bedi, 23, who represented Central Delhi Kings and had earlier been part of the Chennai Super Kings squad in the 2025 IPL, followed protocol by promptly flagging the approach. The DDCA has formally informed the Board of Control for Cricket in India and sought its guidance. No other official complaints were lodged with the ACU, the official added. DDCA Secretary Ashok Sharma said Bedi reported an approach from a player from Uttar Pradesh who was also playing in a T20 league in that state. The association underlined that security liaison officers had been deployed with every team and described its anti-corruption arrangements as “watertight.” In a statement, the DDCA termed the broader allegations emerging from the Tehelka investigation “unverified” and cautioned against drawing conclusions about any player or franchise solely on the basis of such reports. It confirmed it had written to the relevant authorities requesting a proper examination of the matter. Bedi has denied any link to the match-fixing claims made in the sting, describing certain reports associating him with them as false and defamatory, and said his legal team was pursuing action. Published in Dawn, September 23rd, 2026

items.title: Rs17.2bn project launched to boost climate resilience in GB
items.description: • Scheme to benefit 43,200 households across region • Energy master plan unveiled to address power deficit GILGIT: The Agence Française de Développement (AFD), Gilgit-Baltistan (GB) government, Euro­pean Union (EU) and Aga Khan Foundation (AKF) on Tuesday launched a €54.24 million (Rs17.2 billion) project to strengthen climate resilience and improve living conditions across the region. The Gilgit-Baltistan Rural Devel­opment and Climate Resilience (GBRDCR) project, supported through AFD financing, an EU grant, AKF funding and community contributions, will focus on climate-resilient infrastructure, basic services, renewable energy and institutional development. The agreement was signed at the GB Chief Minister’s Secretariat by Additional Chief Secretary Riaz Ahmed, AFD Country Director Marc-Antoine Leclercq and AKF CEO Akhtar Iqbal. CM Amjad Hussain, EU Ambas­sador to Pakistan Raimundas Karo­blis, Senior Minister Mohammad Ali Akhtar and Local Government Minister Zulfiqar Ali Murad also attended the ceremony. The initiative will cover all districts of GB and include 216 water and sanitation schemes, which include 117 drinking-water supply schemes and 30 sanitation projects. Hydropower initiatives are exp­e­c­ted to generate 1,200-1,300kW of cle­an energy. The project will also conduct vulnerability assessments acr­oss all 110 union councils, green-retrofit 3,000 households and support energy-efficient, resilient construction for another 700 households. Training will be provided in climate-smart planning, enterprise development and sustainable infrastructure management. The project is expected to reach around 43,200 households, or 325,600 people, with women accounting for at least 40 per cent of beneficiaries. Community participation GB Chief Minister Amjad Hus­sain, addressing the ceremony, said the project would be an important milestone for sustainable development and protecting communities from the effects of climate change. Energy master plan During the event, Northern Pakistan Energy Limited (NPak Energy) presented key findings of the Gilgit-Baltistan Energy Master Plan, a 30-year roadmap developed under the EU-funded €31m (Rs9.8bn) Energy Plus project. The plan seeks to establish a reliable, affordable and climate-resilient energy system while addressing the region’s power deficit and exploi­ting its renewable-energy potential. EU Ambassador Raimundas Karoblis described the launch as a significant step towards a sustainable and resilient future for GB. AFD Country Director Marc-Antoine Leclercq said the project would improve basic services and strengthen the GB government’s institutional capacity to implement community-driven development, particularly in remote areas. Published in Dawn, September 23rd, 2026

items.title: Trump says US, Iran officials held 3-hour meeting in New York
items.description: US President Donald Trump said on Tuesday that his special envoys, Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner, held three-hour talks with Iranian officials on the sidelines of the UN General Debate in New York. "It was a very good meeting," Trump told reporters. "I can't imagine why they wouldn't want to do it," he added, referring to the possibility of a US-Iran deal. "It's potential greatness or obliteration. It's two choices." Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian and Foreign Minister Seyed Abbas Araghchi were in New York to attend UN meetings. Araghchi conveyed the country's "decisive positions" regarding the reopening of the Strait of Hormuz to the United States, state-run IRIB news agency reported. Citing its exclusive source, the IRIB said Iran's positions were relayed to the US side in a meeting between Araghchi and Witkoff on the sidelines of the 81st session of the United Nations General Assembly (UNGA) in New York. According to the report, among Iran's conditions for the waterway's reopening are lifting the US naval blockade, releasing frozen Iranian assets and ending the war in the region on all fronts. Trump also said in his UNGA speech on Tuesday that he has prevented Tehran from obtaining a nuclear weapon and warned that he could "annihilate the Islamic Republic" if no deal is reached to end ‌the conflict. According to vessel-tracking firm Kpler's data, only two commercial vessels transited the Strait of Hormuz on Monday, down from 10 vessels the previous day. (With input from agencies)

US to expand military presence in Greenland under three-way deal
items.description: The US, Denmark and its self-governing territory of Greenland on Tuesday signed an agreement in New York to expand US military presence on the strategic Arctic island. US President Donald Trump, Danish Prime Minister Mette Frederiksen and Greenland's Prime Minister Jens-Frederik Nielsen signed the deal at a ceremony on the sidelines of the UN General Assembly. The United States can modernize and expand its activities at the existing Pituffik Space Base in northwestern Greenland and establish "an additional defense area at Narsarsuaq and Mestersvig." The pact also permits US aircraft to fly over and land anywhere in Greenland, including its territorial waters, and US public vessels may have undersea access and movement within those waters, without restriction except as mutually agreed upon by the parties. It bars non-NATO states from establishing manned or unmanned military installations in Greenland, or maintaining a persistent military presence there, unless otherwise agreed. It also restricts states or investors from outside NATO, NATO partner countries and the EU from gaining control, significant influence or access to non-public information that could threaten national security or public order in sensitive sectors or activities on the island. The deal came after months of pressure from Trump, who repeatedly called for acquiring the self-governing Danish territory and did not rule out military or economic means. The proposal drew strong opposition from NATO allies and Greenlanders. Under a 1951 defense agreement between Denmark and the United States, amended in 2004, the US military has rights to station personnel and to build, maintain and operate facilities in designated defense areas in Greenland, including Pituffik Space Base. The new agreement enters into force once the Kingdom of Denmark, together with Greenland, has completed the necessary parliamentary procedures and delivered a diplomatic note informing Washington.

items.title: « Des blindés français payés à près de 500 millions » : Le Capitaine Ibrahim Traoré démontre la réalité de l’assemblage militaire
items.description: Face aux réserves exprimées sur la capacité du Burkina Faso à concevoir et assembler ses propres véhicules militaires, le Président de la Transition, le Capitaine Ibrahim Traoré, remet les réalités industrielles et économiques au cœur du débat. En s'appuyant sur les chiffres des acquisitions militaires et le fonctionnement du marché mondial de la défense, le Chef de l'État démontre que l'ingénierie nationale et l'adaptation locale constituent la seule voie vers l'autonomie stratégique. Dans son analyse de la situation sécuritaire et industrielle, le Capitaine Ibrahim Traoré est revenu sur le coût élevé des équipements militaires importés dans la sous-région. Évoquant l'exemple de blindés comme le Bastion de conception française acquis à près de 500 millions l'unité à travers plusieurs pays francophones , le Chef de l'État a interrogé la viabilité à long terme d'un modèle reposant exclusivement sur l'achat à l'étranger. Selon lui, consacrer des ressources massives à l'importation sans développer de capacités nationales de maintenance et d'adaptation condamne les États à une dépendance structurelle. Pour répondre aux critiques contestant la valeur de l'assemblage local, le Président du Faso a rappelé le fonctionnement réel de l'industrie automobile et de défense à l'échelle internationale. Aucun constructeur mondial ne produit l'intégralité de ses composants de A à Z : Les firmes automobiles comme Mercedes ou BMW font appel à des sous-traitants spécialisés pour les pneumatiques, le vitrage, l'électronique ou la câblerie. L'engin blindé Casspir (Afrique du Sud) intègre une motorisation Mercedes. Le blindé français Bastion est propulsé par des moteurs britanniques Perkins ou Cummins. Le VAB français utilise des moteurs allemands MAN. Le Bushmaster australien s'appuie sur des composants Caterpillar. L'intégration de sous-ensembles issus de différents fournisseurs spécialisés constitue la norme mondiale de la construction mécanique. Au-delà de la provenance des pièces, la valeur ajoutée stratégique réside dans la conception et l'adaptation au théâtre d'opérations. Démarré en 2023, le programme burkinabè de conception de blindés repose sur un travail d'ingénierie visant à adapter la structure, le blindage et la mobilité des engins aux contraintes spécifiques du terrain et de la guerre asymétrique. En maîtrisant la chaîne d'assemblage et de modification, le Burkina Faso entend garantir la pérennité de son matériel tout en valorisant les compétences scientifiques et techniques locales. « Il y a des choses qu’on ne veut jamais apprendre au noir » : Le Capitaine Ibrahim Traoré appelle à créer nos propres technologies
items.description: Lors d'une audience accordée aux lauréates du concours de détection de talents scientifiques féminins « HAKILI Mousso », le Président du Faso, le Camarade Capitaine Ibrahim Traoré, a délivré une adresse axée sur la souveraineté et le développement. Élargissant la réflexion au-delà des seules infrastructures physiques, le Chef de l'État a plaidé pour un changement de paradigme fondé sur la valorisation des ressources humaines, la maîtrise technologique et la transformation locale des richesses. Recevant les lauréates du concours « HAKILI Mousso », une initiative dédiée à la promotion des talents scientifiques féminins, le Président du Faso, le Camarade Capitaine Ibrahim Traoré, a exposé sa vision de l'édification nationale. Pour le Chef de l'État, associer le développement uniquement à l'érection de grands immeubles ou de réseaux routiers relève d'une conception erronée. Il a affirmé que le véritable développement débute par la qualité de la ressource humaine. Sortir du piège du salariat capitalistique Mettant en garde contre la dépendance exclusive vis-à-vis des investissements directs étrangers, le Capitaine Ibrahim Traoré a souligné qu'un pays reposant uniquement sur des capitaux extérieurs cantonne ses citoyens au rôle de simples employés d'un système capitalistique. Selon lui, si la mondialisation venait à s'interrompre et que les investisseurs retiraient leurs capitaux, l'absence de production propre révélerait un déficit réel de développement. Face à ce constat, le Burkina Faso choisit de tracer sa propre voie en s'appuyant sur ses compétences internes. Souveraineté technologique et quête de respect international Analysant la géopolitique et les récents conflits mondiaux, le Président du Faso a défendu la nécessité de bâtir une relative autarcie afin de garantir la continuité de la vie nationale en cas de fermeture du monde, tout en restant ouvert aux échanges. Il a dénoncé les entraves au transfert de technologies vers l'Afrique et le préjugé réduisant le Noir au statut de consommateur. Pour imposer le respect et amener les partenaires internationaux à coopérer sur des bases équitables, le Chef de l'État a exhorté à produire, créer et transformer localement les ressources disponibles. items.title: 81e AG de l’ONU : Le Burkina Faso, le Mali et le Niger coordonnent leur action pour porter la voix de l’AES
items.description: À New York, les trois pays membres de la Confédération des États du Sahel préparent une participation coordonnée à la 81e session de l’Assemblée générale des Nations unies, avec notamment un événement parallèle consacré à l’AES. Le Burkina Faso, le Mali et le Niger accordent leurs positions à New York à l’occasion de la 81e session de l’Assemblée générale des Nations unies. Les ministres des Affaires étrangères des trois pays et leurs représentants diplomatiques à Washington et à New York ont tenu, dimanche 21 septembre 2026, une réunion préparatoire en vue de coordonner leur participation à ce rendez-vous diplomatique mondial. La 81e session de l’Assemblée générale de l’ONU s’ouvre ce mardi 22 septembre 2026 à New York. Pour la Confédération des États du Sahel (AES), cette rencontre constitue une occasion de présenter les positions et les priorités des trois États membres sur la scène multilatérale. Une participation coordonnée des trois pays La réunion préparatoire a notamment permis aux délégations de passer en revue le programme de la session et de s’accorder sur les principaux éléments devant guider leurs interventions. Cette coordination doit également concerner l’événement parallèle consacré à la Confédération des États du Sahel, qui sera animé par les chefs de la diplomatie du Burkina Faso, du Mali et du Niger. L’objectif affiché est d’assurer une cohérence dans les différentes prises de parole des trois pays et de porter une position commune sur les questions concernant l’espace confédéral. « Le seul mot d’ordre, c’est d’agir dans le sens de la consolidation de la Confédération AES, c’est aussi d’agir dans le sens de la continuité de la bataille pour la correction des narratifs sur l’espace confédéral. Nous sommes là pour porter la voix de l’AES nous-mêmes et ne pas laisser d’autres acteurs parler à notre place », a déclaré le ministre burkinabè des Affaires étrangères, Karamoko Jean Marie Traoré. Cette démarche s’inscrit dans la volonté affichée par les trois États de renforcer leur coordination diplomatique. En juin 2026, les ministres des Affaires étrangères du Burkina Faso, du Mali et du Niger s’étaient déjà réunis à Bamako pour renforcer l’action diplomatique commune de la Confédération. Le ministre Karamoko Jean Marie Traoré donne ses orientations à la délégation burkinabè Avant la réunion tripartite, le ministre Karamoko Jean Marie Traoré a rencontré les membres de la délégation burkinabè à la Mission permanente du Burkina Faso auprès des Nations unies à New York. Au cours de cette rencontre, le chef de la diplomatie burkinabè a donné des orientations aux membres de la délégation afin que leur participation à la 81e Assemblée générale corresponde aux instructions des autorités burkinabè. Il a également félicité les chefs des missions diplomatiques du Burkina Faso à Washington et à New York pour le travail effectué en amont de la session. Karamoko Jean Marie Traoré a enfin appelé les membres de la délégation à privilégier l’esprit d’équipe et l’engagement, afin d’assurer une participation coordonnée du Burkina Faso aux travaux de l’Assemblée générale. L’AES au cœur de l’agenda diplomatique à New York La Confédération des États du Sahel doit ainsi occuper une place dans les échanges diplomatiques des trois pays à New York. Le Mali a notamment confirmé que l’AES sera au cœur de sa diplomatie multilatérale, avec un événement parallèle dédié à la Confédération. La participation des trois États intervient dans la continuité des efforts engagés pour renforcer leur coordination diplomatique et défendre des positions communes sur la scène internationale. En 2025 déjà, les ministres des Affaires étrangères de l’AES avaient tenu plusieurs concertations à New York en marge de l’Assemblée générale de l’ONU. items.title: Prévention des risques professionnels : Le numérique au cœur des nouveaux enjeux de la 10e édition du SYAPRO
items.description: Le Ministre d’Etat, Ministre de l’Administration territoriale et de la Mobilité, le Camarade Emile ZERBO, représentant le Premier Ministre, Chef du Gouvernement, le Camarade Rimtalba Jean Emmanuel OUEDRAOGO, a présidé, le mardi 22 septembre 2026, à Ouagadougou, la cérémonie officielle d’ouverture de la 10e édition du Symposium sur l’Audiovisuel et la Prévention des Risques professionnels de Ouagadougou (SYAPRO). Placée sous le thème : « Prévention des risques professionnels à l’ère de l’économie numérique : impacts, défis et perspectives », cette édition s’intéresse aux nouveaux enjeux liés à la transformation numérique du monde du travail. Livrant le discours du Premier Ministre, Chef du Gouvernement, le Ministre d’Etat, le Camarade Emile ZERBO, a rappelé que la santé et la sécurité au travail constituent des composantes essentielles de la protection du capital humain. S’appuyant sur les données de l’Organisation internationale du Travail (OIT), il a indiqué que près de trois millions (3 000 000) de travailleurs perdent chaque année la vie dans l’exercice de leurs fonctions. « Au Burkina Faso, mille deux cent quarante et un (1 241) accidents de travail et maladies professionnelles ont été déclarés à la Caisse nationale de Sécurité sociale (CNSS) et mille cent un (1 101) auprès de la Caisse autonome de Retraite des Fonctionnaires (CARFO) », a-t-il précisé, citant le Premier Ministre. Abordant les mutations liées à l’économie numérique, le Ministre d’Etat, le Camarade Emile ZERBO, a relevé que l’intelligence artificielle, les plateformes digitales, les outils collaboratifs et le télétravail offrent de nouvelles opportunités, mais génèrent également de nouveaux facteurs de risques : hyperconnexion, charge mentale, sédentarité, risques psychosociaux, troubles musculosquelettiques et surcharge cognitive numérique. Dans ce contexte, l’audiovisuel et les nouveaux supports numériques apparaissent comme de puissants leviers de sensibilisation. Réseaux sociaux, vidéos, applications et autres outils digitaux peuvent contribuer à diffuser plus largement la culture de la prévention auprès des travailleurs et des populations. Le Ministre d’Etat, le Camarade Emile ZERBO, a ainsi invité les participants à réfléchir autour de deux questions majeures : « Comment mettre le numérique au service de la prévention des risques professionnels ? Et comment continuer à mener cette prévention avec pertinence, dans un environnement de travail bouleversé par les nouvelles technologies ? » Pour les pouvoirs publics, l’enjeu est de faire de l’innovation technologique un facteur d’amélioration des conditions de travail, tout en préservant la santé et le lien social. « Nous n’accepterons jamais que le progrès technique détruise le lien humain », a-t-il martelé. Pour sa part, le Secrétaire Général de l’Interafricaine de la Prévention des Risques professionnels (IAPRP), Monsieur Mohamed SYLLA, a relevé l’évolution des outils de communication et l’essor des réseaux sociaux, des applications mobiles, de la réalité virtuelle, des plateformes collaboratives et de l’intelligence artificielle. Il a également mis en avant le potentiel du numérique pour améliorer la collecte et l’analyse des données sur les accidents du travail, adapter les messages de prévention et mieux anticiper les risques. Parrain de cette 10e édition, le Président du Conseil d’Administration de Coris Holding, le Camarade Idrissa NASSA, a, quant à lui, placé l’être humain au cœur de la responsabilité de l’entreprise. « La prévention des risques professionnels n’est pas une défense, mais un investissement dans la pérennité, la performance et le capital humain de l’entreprise », a-t-il souligné.
